acceptance: The guide explains baseline construction, runner-class consistency, how to choose --fail-on-regression and the two minimum-delta options from measured spread, and how to branch on the distinct exit codes.
The guide states the detection limits with the worked numbers from the sensitivity review, for example a small query that doubles yet stays under the per-query floor.

The example workflow is exercised in BenchBox CI against a fixture, or the nightly perf step is shown to use the same commands; either way the PR shows a passing run and a deliberately regressed run failing with the regression exit code.
No statement in the guide contradicts docs/internal/perf-smoke.md after the review; the PR lists the checked points.
The guide is published in the site documentation and linked from compare's help text or reference page.
context:
Origin: adversarial review on 2026-11-13 of work first left unfiled. The earlier reasons assumed a person at the keyboard; this item records the corrected disposition. Line numbers are hints; re-read the cited file before relying on them.

Why it waits: the nightly gate's baseline and floors are being rebuilt (perf-smoke-rebaseline-after-power-query-generation-20261103, then the sensitivity review). A recipe published before that would teach the old numbers' method.

Decision gate (first step): read both internal documents and the review's ruling. If the review concludes the method is not sound enough to recommend to users, stop and ask the owner to drop this item. An earlier sketch proposed running base and head in the same job instead of a stored baseline; adopt it only if the review endorses it, and say which design was chosen and why.

There is no evidence yet that users want this; priority is low for that reason.

Verification rubric: pass only if both the passing and the failing run are shown and the limits section carries real numbers.

Guardrails: work only in a linked worktree (make worktree-create, then make agent-write-preflight); never edit the primary clone. One PR per item, squash-merged to develop (site work: one PR in BenchBox-dev/benchbox-site). Add a changelog.d fragment for any user-facing change. No live-cloud runs and no credentials in Git or logs. Heavy work (benchmarks, test tiers) runs only through lock-taking entry points or make heavy-run after make heavy-status. Follow the comment policy (make comment-policy-check). Stop and report instead of widening scope; scope removed during review must be re-homed to a named item or dropped by the owner with a reason.
description:
Problem: BenchBox has worked out how to gate on performance in CI: a stored baseline built from medians over at least five runs on one runner class, floors derived from measured spread, and no baseline from a single local run. That knowledge sits in docs/internal/perf-smoke.md, docs/internal/nightly-perf-gate-review.md and scripts/perf_smoke_baseline.py and is not published. A person, or an agent asked to 'add a performance check', has nothing to copy and will write a naive single-run comparison.

Outcome: a user-facing guide and one example GitHub Actions workflow that follow the same method BenchBox's own nightly uses once the sensitivity review has ruled, including what the gate cannot detect.

Non-goals: no packaged GitHub Action; no new comparison features; no change to BenchBox's own floors or baseline.
